issues.description: Method simulate (Exercise 1) has inconsistent expected return types across artifacts. Problem statement (problem_statement.md) Exercise 1.6 instructs students to "Simulate the circuit and return the statevector" (line 116). The template implementation (template_repository/ex1_grover_two_qubit_without_auxiliary_qubit.py) declares simulate as def simulate(self, qc: QuantumCircuit) -> dict[str, int]: (signature at line 52) which indicates measurement counts, and the body is a stub. The reference solution (solution_repository/ex1_grover_two_qubit_without_auxiliary_qubit.py) implements simulate as def simulate(self, qc: QuantumCircuit) -> list[complex]: (signature at line 61) and returns a statevector. This return-type mismatch (template: dict[str,int] vs problem+solution: statevector/list[complex] or Statevector) will confuse students about what to implement and may cause them to produce the wrong kind of output for tests or exercises.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template's simulate method signature and documentation with the problem statement and solution. Update the template simulate signature to return a statevector (e.g., -> list[complex] or -> qiskit.quantum_info.Statevector) and update imports/docstring accordingly to explicitly state that a statevector is expected. Example actionable steps: (1) change the signature in template_repository/ex1_grover_two_qubit_without_auxiliary_qubit.py to def simulate(self, qc: QuantumCircuit) -> list[complex]: (or -> Statevector) ; (2) update the docstring to say "Return the statevector (qiskit Statevector or list of complex amplitudes)"; (3) if choosing Statevector, add the appropriate import in the template; (4) ensure any tests or instructions reference the same return type. This preserves the educational intent (students should return the statevector) and removes ambiguity between counts vs. statevector.
